Positioning statement, internal: not public copy

ONE Mahjong is the only American mahjong card committed to opening its whole structure, every hand design and how hands are made, so no single organization controls the game's hands; its cards are free and new every season, and one set that plays every kind of mahjong is in the works.

How it looks

Headlines are set in a friendly slab with large, unambiguous digits, and running text in a rounded, open sans. The signature layout pairs a close photograph of real tiles with a soft card that holds actual hands, each with its reading in plain words beneath it. Photographs are real, licensed and credited, and they show the tiles up close. Corners are soft. Motion is short and gentle; nothing bounces. The card a player prints at home is ink only on plain white paper, Letter or A4. A full colour flood streaks and drains a home printer, and the card must read the same from any printer in black. The lockup, the section, the hands and the independence notice keep their places; rules between hands print as thin grey lines.

How colour is used

ONE Mahjong looks like the room where the game is already set up and someone has kept a chair for you. The ground is a soft peach, a pale tint of the hue of an old butterscotch tile, and panels sit lighter, like a card laid on a table. Text is a warm charcoal, with secondary text a shade softer. The one action colour is eucalyptus, the quiet green of the leaves painted on old flower tiles. The dark theme is an evening version of the same room, never a black screen. The ground is a soft brown, panels sit a step lighter, text is a warm off-white, and the action turns a pale eucalyptus.

A comfortable chair, kept for you

Clear space and minimum size

The mark is an armchair in three-quarter view, drawn in one ink. It stands for the idea behind the brand: there's always a seat for you. Use it in one colour (charcoal on the light ground, off-white on the dark ground). It is never outlined, tilted, recoloured in parts or set inside a container shape. The name beside it is the drawn ONE Mahjong wordmark, never retyped in the font. Minimum size: the mark at 32 px, the lockup at 32 px tall. Clear space: a quarter of the mark's height on every side, kept free of type, edges and other marks. On a dark ground use the on-dark files; never recolour the mark in the brand colour on a busy picture.

Voiceself-aware and playful: the table in second person, present tense, with its literal facts (four copies, plain paper, the Charleston, the snack table)
Pairsplayful, never silly about the rules; warm, never sugary; open about how the card is made, never preachy about who owns the game; cheeky about the annual fee, never rude about the League
Person"you" and "your table" for the players; "we" for the people who build the card; the card is the subject in feature lines
Sentencesmostly 6 to 16 words; one longer sentence where the data needs explaining; numbers as digits with their unit
Humoura straight face about table life (jokers, snacks, the wall, the Charleston) with the fact right under the joke, in sub-lines, section notes and microcopy; none in the research numbers, the independence notice or anything about the League
NeverLeague names, initials or marks; "open source" or "published" about the structure before it ships; a buy button, a price or a ship date for the set before it is on sale; the incumbent's price; motive words (scam, racket, greedy, cartel, tax as an accusation); "largest ever"; the held gap figure; praise words about ourselves; "free" on the paid set; a joke aimed at a player or at the League

Before launch

Still to settle

Open questions for the owner

  • The open card structure has no licence chosen yet; nothing may call it "open source" until one is.
  • The positioning statement's claim to be the only such card rests on one search, on 2026-11-21; check it again before that claim appears in public copy.
  • No trademark search has been run for "ONE Mahjong" (classes 9, 16, 28, 41); do one before any filing or paid launch.
  • The League's terms of use were not read; have counsel read them before the first card ships.
  • The hero photograph shows real tiles but not an American home game, because no openly licensed photo of one passed; a commissioned photo of a real table would serve the brand better.
  • The armchair and "There's always a seat for you." were screened on 2026-11-23 and no conflict turned up. The live USPTO search, EU registers and reverse-image search could not run, so do those before any filing.
  • The nearest name is Mahjong One, a tile-matching puzzle app. Decide whether that is close enough to matter before the trademark search.
  • The flower photograph is CC BY-SA 4.0. Whether a poster built on it must itself be shared alike needs a legal reading before public use.
